questions.q: OpenAI's text-embedding-3-small and text-embedding-3-large have which dimensions, and what storage escape hatch does the 3-series offer?
options: 1536 and 3072; dimension truncation (e.g., request 512 dims from the large model) with modest quality loss
384 and 1024; native int8 outputs only
3072 and 6144; binary embeddings
768 and 1536; multi-vector indexes
questions.explain: The chapter gives 1,536 dims for text-embedding-3-small and 3,072 for text-embedding-3-large, and notes the 3-series supports requesting fewer dimensions (truncation) to trade storage/index size against quality without changing models.

questions.q: What is Cohere's input_type parameter, and what contract must you honor?
options: It enables streaming; you must checkpoint batches
It chooses the distance metric; you must match it in CREATE VECTOR INDEX
It selects the output dimension; you must use the same dimension at query time

It tunes the embedding for its role — search_document vs search_query — and documents embedded as search_document must be queried with search_query vectors, enforced with the ModelName column plus an input-type column
questions.explain: Cohere's input_type (search_document vs search_query) tunes embeddings for asymmetric retrieval; the chapter requires honoring it in both directions, enforced via the ModelName column plus an input-type column when both roles share a table.

questions.q: When comparing models, what is the first axis the chapter says to evaluate on, in order?
options: Per-1K-token API price
Public MTEB leaderboard rank
Quality on your data — score candidates on your own versioned eval set of 50–100 questions, not public benchmarks
Vendor release recency
questions.explain: The chapter orders the axes: quality on your data first (MTEB is generic; your corpus is not — build the Chapter 22.8 eval harness), then total cost, then latency profile; a smaller domain-savvy model routinely beats a larger general one.

questions.q: The column width changes with the model (VECTOR(384) for MiniLM, VECTOR(1024) for BGE). What does this imply about a model change?
options: It only requires updating the ModelName default
It is a schema migration handled side-by-side: add a second vector column, throttled backfill, new DiskANN index, switch query path, then drop the old column
It is a simple in-place ALTER COLUMN
You can mix both models in one column safely
questions.explain: Because the dimension is part of the schema, a model change is a full re-ingestion event — never in-place: side-by-side second vector column, throttled backfill, new index, verified eval scores, then drop the old column.

questions.q: float32 vectors cost 4 bytes per dimension. What is the correct SQL Server query pattern for estimating vector storage per model from the chapter?
options: SUM(datalength(Embedding))
sp_spaceused per model
COUNT(*) * 1536 with no byte factor
COUNT(*) * 1536 * 4 / 1024 / 1024 AS ApproxVectorMB_1536d grouped by ModelName
questions.explain: The chapter's storage query computes COUNT(*) * dimension * 4 bytes converted to MB per ModelName (e.g., COUNT(*) * 1536 * 4 / 1024 / 1024), noting float32 = 4 bytes/dimension, refined with sys.dm_db_partition_stats for row overhead and indexes.
